b: I manage a fully remote employee, Paul, who is not doing well, and I suspect he’s using a mouse jiggler to keep his mouse moving so he appears more available than he is.

I have been talking to Paul about the issues I am seeing with his performance, one of which is responsiveness. He is so unresponsive that other team members come to me to report they haven’t heard from him for hours. I have had to jump in to assure his colleagues that something is being handled when a deadline is fast approaching and they can’t get ahold of Paul. Someone even joked with me that they suspect he has a second job. Also, this is not workload-related; to the contrary, he is under-allocated and does not have a full workload.

I first talked to Paul about this issue a few months ago and told him that I do not want to wade into policing how he spends his time, but he should give me a heads-up if he needs to be unavailable for an extended period of time. In my head, I was thinking doctor’s appointments or things of that nature. He has since pinged me for a variety of activities that take him away from his desk that don’t feel particularly legitimate, like “I need to step out to run to the store.” Here’s the thing: If you haven’t used your computer for a while, our chat system turns your chat bubble red to indicate you’re not available (it’s green when you’re there and working). During these errands, his chat bubble stays green, indicating he’s “available” even when he’s just told me he’ll be away. I have pinged him with questions 30 minutes to an hour later and his response can take up to 90 minutes from when he let me know he’s stepping away. Again, green bubble the whole time, which makes me think he’s set something up to make his computer appear to be in use when it’s not, such as a mouse jiggler.

We had a second conversation where I once again addressed his response time, but I don’t think I hit on the real point I was trying to get across. I let him know that I was glad he was letting me know when he was stepping out and that our workplace is okay with flexibility, but people are still reaching out to me with questions because they can’t reach him. It has improved slightly, but not even to the level of “meets expectations” yet.

I know that the best thing to do is to focus on outcomes, but I’m struggling to do that. I feel like I have focused on the outcomes and it’s not sinking in. My manager advised against me giving him specific time metrics. I wanted to say that he needs to respond to pings within 30 minutes to one hour if he is not in a meeting (and he’s not in many meetings), but she felt like that’s getting too nitpicky. So I’m left with just “be more responsive” but it’s too nebulous. I want to address the weirdness of him telling me that he’s not doing a work task and his chat status still showing him as available, but how do I do that without getting into micromanager territory?

Is it worth asking about the suspected mouse jiggler? Or should I just keep honing in on the responsiveness issue as a whole? Honestly, I’m going back to the joke a coworker made about him having a second job and thinking maybe there’s something to it.
You can read my answer to this letter at New York Magazine.
